_history.why: The full-archive run of 2026-09-29 (207,912 filings, commit e4e78a95) measured 261,460 exact-key duplicate rows on (accession, cik, holder_name, share_class) = 9.00% of 2,903,798 rows, 32.65% in 2009, 19.93% in 2018, 18.75% in 2024, against 248/250 spot-checked values exact. The values are right and the rows are over-emitted, and NO existing gate can see it: all five read gold-linked filings only, and the gold sets are vendor coverage of larger filers that does not reach 1994-1995 or 2025-2026 at all.
_history.diagnosis_before_the_threshold: Measured on the full panel with duckdb before any threshold was written. The 261,460 excess rows decompose EXACTLY into 244,792 same-`table_kind` (8.430% of rows — over-emission) and 16,668 cross-`table_kind` (0.574% — the same holder listed in the 5% table AND the management table, which the document really does). Same-kind splits again into 125,576 inside ONE table_index (4.324%) and 119,216 across table_index of the same kind (4.106%). So (i) is 8.43%, far above the 1.0% gate, and the round is warranted. Cross-kind is REPORTED, never gated: gating it would pay the loop to suppress a legitimate disclosure.
_history.mechanisms: Named from -debug on 12 of the worst 2009 / 2018 / 2024 filings. (1) MULTI-CLASS VALUE COLUMNS WITH AN EMPTY share_class — 108,592 of 125,576 within-one-table excess rows (86.5%) carry share_class='' — e.g. 0001104659-24-052085 (Liberty Media) emits 9 correct rows for John C. Malone, one per series, all with share_class empty because the row-level `Title of Series` column is roled `other`; 0001258602-24-000028 (Nelnet) pairs the Total and combined-voting-power columns without a class label. (2) A `Title of Class` column taken as the NAME column — 0001683863-24-008416 emits holder_name 'Admiral Shares' / 'Investor Shares'. (3) NON-OWNERSHIP TABLES ATTACHED once per fund in fund-family proxies — 0000051931-09-000935 / -18-000890 (American Funds) read director COMPENSATION dollars as `shares` across dozens of per-fund tables. (4) The ASCII text path glues the fund-class label to the holder name — 0000932471-09-000972 emits 'Investor Shares: Charles Schwab & Co'. The unifying root cause is that the class / series identity is never carried into `share_class`, so rows that ARE distinct collapse onto one exact key. The fix is to POPULATE share_class, not to suppress rows.
_history.guard: The five pre-existing gates plus the new per-year yield floor are the guard: the duplicate ceilings can be cleared by suppressing rows, and suppression drives holder_recall_blockw under 0.75, iss_director_recall under 0.82, filing_yield_parsed_percent under 0.88, or a single sample year's yield under its recorded floor. A round that deletes rows to clean the key therefore still exits 1.

_history.old_definition: excess rows sharing (accession, cik, holder_name, share_class) WITHIN one table_kind.
_history.new_definition: excess copies of an IDENTICAL ROW: same (accession, cik, table_kind, holder_name, share_class, shares, percent). `shares` and `percent` are compared as the parser emitted them, because a row emitted twice by one parse emits byte-identical numbers. table_index is deliberately OUT of the key, so one row emitted from two tables of the same kind still counts as a duplicate.
_history.why: The old key counted legitimately distinct rows as duplicates. One holder listed once per managed account, each row carrying its OWN shares and percent, collapses onto (holder, class, kind) — AllianceBernstein's 2018 proxy is the type case: 264 of that year's 304 remaining excess rows, and 620 of the 4,352 excess rows remaining across the sample. Two journal floors had already been recorded against exactly this, `one-record-holder-many-accounts-one-fund-class` and `sample_dup_excess_same_table_rate_max_year-2018-unreachable`: the loop had proved the 2018 ceiling unreachable WITHOUT deleting true rows, which is a defect in the metric and not in the parser. An identical row is a duplicate under any reading, so the new key admits no such floor. BOTH journal floors are superseded by this entry.
_history.kept_as_diagnostic: `sample_dup_excess_same_table_rate` and `_max_year` are reported alongside the gated pair every round, so the redefinition is visible in the printout and in metrics_dev.json rather than being a silently easier gate. The per-year table prints dup_ident and dup_same side by side, and sample_by_year.tsv carries both.
_history.guard: Unchanged, and it still binds: the identical-row ceilings can be cleared by suppressing rows, and suppression drives holder_recall_blockw under 0.75, iss_director_recall under 0.82, filing_yield_parsed_percent under 0.88, or a single sample year's yield under its recorded floor. Widening the duplicate definition does not touch that argument — it only stops the ceiling from PAYING for suppression of rows that were never duplicates.

_sample_floors_note: Per-year parsed-percent yield floors on the fixed full-archive sample (gold/sample_full.tsv, seed 20260929). Each value is the yield MEASURED AT HEAD on that year minus 0.005 of slack, recorded once by a human with `score.py --record-sample-floors`. `sample_yield_worst_year_margin` = min over years of (measured yield - floor) and is gated at 0.0, so no single year may regress by more than the slack while the duplicate gate is being closed. An EMPTY object here means the floors have not been recorded; score.py then cannot compute the gated margin and exits with a message saying so, rather than scoring a gate over a floor it invented.
